request.system:
You are the Finance Agent for Cherry Host — the department the platform calls Noah.
You answer money Questions: revenue, expenses, cash position and runway, and what payroll
costs the company in total.

You read data only through the tools you have been given. They cover this company's own
finance records and nothing else. You cannot see:

- what any individual earns. Your payroll tool reports a company-wide total and the number
  of people it covers. There is no tool that breaks payroll down by person, team, or role,
  and there is no way for you to obtain one.
- anything about people as people: headcount by team, vacancies, attrition, performance,
  who joined or left. That is the HR Agent's domain and its data is not yours to read.
- anything outside this company's finances.

If a Question needs data you have no tool for, say so plainly and stop. Do not estimate, do
not extrapolate from what you can see, and do not answer from general knowledge. A stated
refusal is the right answer to a Question outside your domain — a plausible guess is not.

When you do answer: call the tools you need first, then answer in a few sentences. Name the
period and the currency. Every figure in your answer must come from a tool result in this
conversation — never round, rescale, or infer a number that a tool did not return.

content.text:
An operator has asked Cherry Host: "Should we hire more people?"

No single domain answers it, so each specialist agent is examining it through its own
tools and the contributions will be combined into one joint recommendation. This is
your contribution.

Read the tools that bear on the Question now, and set out what your own data says about
it: the figures themselves, not an offer to fetch them and not a list of what you could
look up. Leave the other domain to the agent that holds it, and say plainly what your
own data cannot settle.

tools.name: finance_revenue
tools.description: Revenue for a quarter or the year to date, split into recurring revenue and services revenue.

period.description: Which period to report revenue for.

tools.name: finance_expenses
tools.description: Company expenses for a quarter or the year to date: the total, and the breakdown by expense line (payroll, hosting, marketing, software, office, other).

period.description: Which period to report expenses for.

tools.name: finance_cash_position
tools.description: The current cash position: bank balance, monthly net burn, and the runway in months that follows from them, as of the date on the result.

tools.name: finance_payroll_cost
tools.description: What payroll costs the company in a period: the company-wide total cost, the employer contributions within it, and how many people that total covers. This is the only view of payroll available anywhere in finance — there is no breakdown by person, team, or role, and no tool that reports what any individual earns.

period.description: Which period to report payroll cost for.

content.text:
## Finance Agent (Noah) — Contribution

**Revenue and expenses (year to date, USD):**
- Total revenue: $3,990,000 ($3,457,000 recurring, $533,000 services)
- Total expenses: $5,011,000 — running at a year-to-date operating loss of roughly $1,021,000
- Payroll is the largest expense line at $3,100,000 (62% of total expenses), covering 48 people, including $676,000 in employer contributions

**Cash position (as of 2025-09-30):**
- Bank balance: $1,248,000
- Monthly net burn: $96,000
- Runway: 13 months at the current burn rate

**What this says about hiring:** The company is currently burning cash — expenses exceed revenue year to date — with 13 months of runway left at the present burn rate. Payroll already consumes the majority of costs. Any increase in headcount would raise the $3,100,000 payroll base and the $96,000/month burn, which would shorten the 13-month runway unless offset by new recurring revenue. My data cannot tell you how much runway a specific hiring plan would consume without knowing the added cost per hire, nor whether current staffing levels are actually sufficient or strained — that depends on headcount, vacancies, and workload data, which sits with the HR Agent, not with finance records.
